title: Routing, Page Titles & Focus Management 🧭
description: Manage document title, focus on navigation, and create skip links in a single‑page app.

slides.title: The SPA Navigation Problem 🗺️
slides.content:
When a user clicks a link in a traditional site, the page reloads, the screen reader reads the new title, and focus goes to the top of the body. In an SPA, the content just swaps – the user may hear nothing, and focus may stay on the link.

We need to manage three things on every route change:
1. **Document title** (so the browser tab and screen reader announce the new page).
2. **Focus** (move it to a logical place, usually the top of the new content).
3. **Announcement** (confirm the navigation to screen reader users).

quizData.question: After a route change in an SPA, what is the minimum you should update for accessibility?

options.text: The document title and manage focus

quizData.explanation: Without title update and focus management, users are lost.

options.text: Screen readers announce the title when focus moves to the page, confirming navigation

quizData.explanation: The title is the first thing announced, helping users orient themselves.

options.text: Non‑focusable elements like `<h1>` need it to receive focus

quizData.explanation: `tabindex='-1'` makes a normally non‑focusable element programmatically focusable without adding it to the tab order.

slides.title: Skip Links in SPAs 🔗
slides.content:
Skip links still apply. Place a skip link at the very beginning of your root component (e.g., App.vue, App.js). Ensure it links to the `id` of the main content container, which should exist in every route view.

Because skip links rely on `href`, they work even without JavaScript if the target exists.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Use a navigation announcer component
Many design systems (like Reach Router, Angular CDK) have a built‑in route announcer. Use it or create a simple one.
